chunks: The Commander of the Faithful عليه السلام said:

If there is an Imam who has gone forward in the salat (prayer) while he is junub, having forgotten, or he experiences hadath, or a nosebleed, or a stirring in his stomach, then he should place his garment over his nose, then withdraw. He should take the hand of a man, and let him pray in his place. Then he should perform wudu (ablution) and complete what of the salat (prayer) had preceded him; and if he was junub, then let him perform ghusl (ritual bath) and pray the whole salat (prayer).

key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the one leading the congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the ritual prayer being led in congregation
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.حَدَثًا: a state of minor ritual impurity that breaks wudu

ai.seo_question: What should an Imam do if he loses ritual purity while leading congregational salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for an Imam who becomes unable to continue leading the congregational salat (prayer) due to ritual impurity, nosebleed, or stomach disturbance. He should leave discreetly, appoint another man to continue the prayer, and then purify himself. If the cause was minor impurity, he completes what remains; if he was in janabah, he performs ghusl and repeats the entire prayer.
